People Operations Associate – Recruitment Coordinator

Job Profile: People Operations

As a Recruitment Coordinator, you'll help deliver a thoughtful, efficient, and seamless candidate experience. You'll partner closely with recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, and candidates to coordinate interviews, support recruiting programs, and improve the operational processes that enable Stripe to hire strong talent.

· Partner with recruiters to coordinate interviews and deliver a high-quality candidate experience throughout the hiring process

· Manage interview scheduling and logistics for candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers

· Communicate clearly and professionally with candidates to ensure they are prepared for interviews and have the information they need

· Support on-site interviews by welcoming candidates, coordinating logistics, and resolving issues in real time

· Plan and execute recruiting events, including job fairs, technical talks, partnership events, and other talent engagement activities

· Coordinate event logistics, including travel, catering, swag, vendor coordination, and venue support, as needed

· Support the planning and delivery of internship program events and engagement initiatives for Stripe’s intern community

· Build, document, and improve administrative processes to ensure recruiting operations are efficient and consistent

· Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive candidate and hiring information

· Develop expertise in Stripe recruiting processes and take on increasingly complex responsibilities over time

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

· 0–2 years of experience in recruitment coordination, scheduling, operations, event coordination, customer support, or a similar fast-paced environment

· Strong organizational skills and outstanding attention to detail

· Ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt quickly to changing schedules, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a professional, clear, and candidate-focused approach

· Ability to collaborate effectively with multiple stakeholders, including candidates, recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, and external vendors

· Demonstrated ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment

· Strong operational execution and problem-solving skills, with a commitment to continuous improvement

· Willingness and ability to work flexible shifts between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. based on business needs

· Willingness and ability to travel up to 30% during peak recruiting cycles, as needed

· Experience supporting industry recruiting, high-volume interview scheduling, internship programs, or recruiting events

· Experience using applicant-tracking systems, scheduling tools, or other recruiting operations platforms

· A creative and process-oriented mindset, with an interest in improving workflows and the candidate experience

· Experience partnering with internal stakeholders in a collaborative, service-oriented environment

FV-F Duties: Serves as an entry-level HR Specialist performing basic buy progressively more difficult assignments. Tasks and assignments require the application of HR concepts, principles, regulations and policy. Participates in the application of merit systems principles to attract, develop, manage and retain a high quality and diverse workforce.

Participates in developmental activities to provide the full range of national recruitment, examining, and staffing services for mission critical agency occupations.

Typical duties include conducting job analysis to develop evaluation criteria and crediting plans; utilizing centralized inventories for agency-wide use; rating and ranking applications for a variety of agency mission critical occupations; and assisting in the issuance of referral lists from centralized inventories.

Assignments are performed under the close direction of a supervisor or senior HR specialists. Applies basic HR knowledge and limited experience to perform assigned tasks. Coordinates with a manager, project/program manager, team leader, or more experienced professional to plan time and use assigned resources to accomplish tasks.

FV-G Duties: Supports the full range of HR products and services to address a wide range of complex, interrelated HRM problems and issues. Locates and identifies qualified candidates for vacancies through competitive and noncompetitive processes.

Advises applicants, employees, and managers on issues of varying complexity concerning recruitment, staffing, and compensation programs.

Typical duties include drafting and building job vacancy announcements for the various/multiple Occupational Job Series, (e.g., 1825, 2101, and 2152) for publishing; generating candidate referral lists; auditing selections ensuring adherence to veteran¿s preference; evaluating applications/résumés for qualifications and adjudicating veteran¿s preference; issuing tentative and firm offer letters (TOL and FOL); initiating personnel actions in Workforce Transformation and Tracking System (WTTS) and processing within Federal Personnel Payroll System (FPPS), and generating reports detailing applicant¿s status of outstanding clearance(s), academy class assignment, TOL/FOL date, etc.

Performs a combination of routine, multiple, and varying assignments under the general direction of a manager, project/program manager, team leader, or more experienced professional. Acts as an individual contributor and/or member of team for projects/programs within a defined area of responsibility.

Participates in development of creative results-driven approaches to recruitment and placement, strategic rewards, continuous learning, and/or employee and labor management relations.

FV-H Duties: In addition to the duties above, provides the full range of HR products and services to address a wide range of complex, interrelated HRM problems and issues. Locates and identifies qualified candidates for vacancies through competitive and noncompetitive processes.

Counsels applicants, employees, and managers on issues of varying complexity concerning recruitment, staffing, and compensation programs.

Supports management in developing workforce by assisting in providing critical training to lower banded HR specialists on HR policies, procedures, information systems, veteran's preference, applicant rating, referring, selection, onboarding, and hiring.

Performs multiple and varying assignments under the limited direction of the supervisor or team leader. May perform some leadership functions for small projects or other work activities.

Demonstrates considerable independence in planning time and helping a manager, project/program manager, and/or team leader to plan and use assigned resources to accomplish projects/programs/activities. May perform other duties as assigned.
To qualify for this position at the FV-F (FG/GS 5-9) level, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess three (3) years of progressively responsible general experience, one (1) year of which was equivalent to at least the GS-4 level that demonstrates the ability to: Analyze problems to identify significant factors, gather pertinent data, and recognize solutions; Plan and organize work; and Communicate effectively.

OR Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in any field leading to a bachelor's degree, in an accredited college or university. OR Combination of education and experience may be qualifying for this position.

To qualify for this position at the FV-G (FG/GS-10/11) level, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to FV-F (GS/FG 5-9) level.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade/band level in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Specialized experience includes: Preparing and publishing vacancy announcements; Reviewing qualification documents and determining applicant eligibility under established qualification standards; Generating referral lists and supporting recruitment actions from announcement through tentative and firm job offers; Initiating and processing personnel actions while ensuring compliance with applicable regulations; and Researching and interpreting HR policies and providing guidance to applicants, employees, and management on staffing and recruitment matters.

OR Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related, in an accredited college or university. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work.

OR Combination of education and experience may be qualifying for this position. To qualify for this position at the FV-H (FG/GS-12) level, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to FV-G (FG/GS-10/11) level.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade/band level in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Specialized experience includes: Providing recruitment, staffing, and placement advisory services to management on complex personnel actions; Independently planning and completing competitive and non-competitive staffing actions from announcement through selection; Interpreting and applying HR laws, regulations, policies, qualification standards, and merit system principles; Resolving complex staffing issues, qualification determinations, and personnel action discrepancies; and Analyzing staffing processes and recommending improvements to enhance recruitment operations.

Applicants should provide examples of specialized experience in their work history. Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

About Docker
Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
_______________________________________________________________________
As a Senior People Partner supporting Revenue at Docker, you will partner closely with leaders, managers, and employees across our go-to-market organization to connect business priorities to people strategy.
This is an experienced individual contributor role for someone who brings strong HR judgment, clear communication, business acumen, and steadiness in complex or high-pressure situations. Revenue is a fast-moving, high-accountability environment, so this person must be able to build trust, influence quickly, and communicate with clarity.

Partner with Revenue leaders and managers on people priorities, including organizational design, workforce planning, leadership effectiveness, talent planning, engagement, performance, and team health.
Provide clear guidance and practical recommendations on complex employee matters, balancing employee experience, business needs, risk, and consistency.
Build trusted relationships across Revenue and within the People Team. Influence through credibility, direct communication, and strong partnership.
Raise concerns, ask hard questions, and push for better decisions when something may pose a risk, create inconsistency, or have an unintended impact.
Stay steady in difficult conversations and bring calm, structure, and sound judgment to situations involving urgency, emotion, competing priorities, or strong opinions.
Lead and support core people processes within Revenue, including performance management, talent reviews, compensation cycles, promotions, employee development, engagement planning, and organizational changes.
Use data, insights, and business context to identify trends, surface risks, and recommend actions that improve team effectiveness, retention, engagement, and performance.
Partner across People, Talent Acquisition, Legal, Finance, People Ops, Total Rewards, and other cross-functional teams to ensure strong alignment and execution for Revenue priorities.
Support global and distributed teams by helping leaders understand regional considerations, cultural norms, and employee experience across different locations.
Contribute to People Team programs and practices by sharing feedback from Revenue, identifying opportunities to improve how we work, and helping build scalable approaches as Docker grows.

Strong experience as a People Partner, HR Business Partner, or similar role, preferably in a technology company or fast-moving global environment.
Experience supporting Revenue, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, or other customer-facing teams is strongly preferred.
Strong HR knowledge across employee relations, performance management, talent management, compensation, organizational design, change management, engagement, and leadership coaching.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex or sensitive information clearly, tailor messages to the audience, and create alignment when stakeholders may not start in the same place.
The ability to push back with confidence and respect. You are comfortable challenging leaders, naming risks, and offering a different perspective when the situation calls for it.
Sound judgment and the ability to navigate complex, sensitive, and ambiguous situations with care, discretion, and a practical understanding of business impact.
Experience supporting global or distributed teams, with an understanding of how to partner across regions, cultures, and time zones.
Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to identify trends, tell a clear story, and recommend action.
A collaborative approach and the ability to work well across People Team functions, Revenue teams, and other internal partners.
What to Expect
In the first month, you will learn Docker’s culture, People Team practices, and the Revenue organization’s business priorities, leadership structure, team dynamics, and current people needs.
In the first three months, you will be actively partnering with Revenue leaders and managers, providing clear guidance, building trust, identifying patterns and risks, and demonstrating sound judgment in sensitive or complex situations.
In the first year, you will be seen as a trusted advisor to Revenue leaders, managers, and employees. You will operate with strong independence, bring leaders recommendations they can act on, and help improve how the Revenue organization approaches leadership, talent, team health, and people decisions.
Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Im Auftrag unseres Mandanten – ein Unternehmen aus der Medizinbranche – suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine engagierte HR-Persönlichkeit in Vollzeit.
Du liebst die Abwechslung zwischen strategischem Gestalten und operativem Anpacken? Du möchtest Führungskräfte auf Augenhöhe beraten, scheust dich aber nicht davor, Verträge selbst aufzusetzen? Dann bist du bei unserem Kunden genau richtig! Als HR Manager / HR Business Partner (m/w/d) bist du die treibende Kraft hinter unserer Personalarbeit – vom täglichen Geschäft bis zur strategischen Weiterentwicklung.
Aufgaben

Du berätst und coachst Führungskräfte in allen Personal- und Führungsfragen.
Du entwickelst HR-Prozesse (z. B. im Recruiting, Talent Management oder Performance-Bereich) strategisch weiter.
Du begleitest Veränderungsprozesse (Change Management) und hilfst den Teams, strukturiert zu wachsen.

Du begleitest den gesamten Employee Life Cycle – vom ersten Vertrag bis zum Zeugnis.
Du betreust das operative Tagesgeschäft und bist Ansprechpartner für die Belegschaft bei täglichen Fragen.
Du pflegst die Personalstammdaten und bereitest die monatliche Gehaltsabrechnung vor.
Qualifikation
Du bringst fundierte Berufserfahrung in der Personalarbeit mit – idealerweise sowohl in der operativen Verwaltung als auch in der Beratung von Führungskräften.
Du besitzt eine ausgeprägte "Hands-on-Mentalität" (du packst gerne selbst an), verlierst dabei aber nie den strategischen Weitblick für das große Ganze.
Du bist kommunikationsstark, empathisch und trittst gegenüber dem Management selbstbewusst und als Sparringspartner auf Augenhöhe auf.
Gute Kenntnisse im deutschen Arbeitsrecht und ein sicherer Umgang mit HR-Software-Tools sind für dich selbstverständlich.

Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag mit 30 Tagen Urlaub und der Möglichkeit zu 1 Tag Home Office in der Woche.
Eine überdurchschnittliche, leistungsgerechte Vergütung sowie zeitgemäße Zusatzleistungen (wie z. B. ein attraktives Fahrradleasing-Programm).
Ein sicherer Arbeitsplatz in einem modernen, innovativen Unternehmen mit hervorragender Infrastruktur.
Individuell auf Sie zugeschnittene Weiterbildungs- und Schulungsangebote zur Förderung Ihrer fachlichen und persönlichen Karriere.
Viel Platz für Eigeninitiative und die Möglichkeit, eigene Ideen in einem wertschätzenden Umfeld direkt umzusetzen.
Ein kollegiales, werteorientiertes Miteinander, das durch regelmäßige Teamevents und gemeinsamen Austausch gestärkt wird.
Haben wir Ihr Interesse geweckt? Als beauftragte Personalberatung freuen wir uns auf Ihre aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen unter Angabe Ihres frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins und Ihrer Gehaltsvorstellung.

Work is to be performed in one or more of the following Health Systems work areas: Tricare, Military Medical Support Office (MMSO), Line of Duty/Incapacitation (LOD/INCAP), Medical Operational Data System (MODS), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Certification, Warrior Transition Unit/Active Duty Medical Extension/Medical Retention Processing (WTU/ADME/MRP2), and Medical boards.

Cases have major effects on career or service as they may result in unfavorable career separation or loss of status. Ensures that regulatory requirements related to the specific action or interviews personnel to obtain needed data.

Coordinates with the Human Resources Command (HRC), National Guard Bureau (NGB), the Military Medical Support Office (MMSO), Tri-Care, Regional Medical Command, the Military Treatment Facilities (MTF), the Medical Evaluation Board (MEB), Physical Evaluation Board Liaison Offices (PEBLO), Regional Army Commands, State and regional counterparts, and members at all unit levels.

Serves as the advisor to the Supervisory Human Resources Specialist on issues of health care, sources of healthcare, and medical aspects of Soldier readiness. Collects, analyzes and provides statistical reports to the Supervisory Human Resources Specialist within the state regarding the health services programs.

As required, organizes, coordinates, and provides briefings and training for workshops, seminars, and conferences. Attends events on behalf of the Supervisory Human Resources Specialist as needed. Manages the funds associated with the appropriate programs and provides accounting for expenditures as required.

Oversees, observes, and advises the release of sensitive information in accordance with HIPAA and Privacy Act standards concerning individual military members and mission requirements.

Coordinates, assembles, monitors and ensures the proper conduct of medical boards, and participates as required. Provides tracking, over-sight, assistance and follow-up to issues identified through all medical aspects of Soldier readiness (SRP, PDHRA, and Periodic Health Assessment (PHA).

Assists with or conducts onsite training as requested or required by supported units and activities. Reviews, evaluates, and interprets regulatory guidance, policies, and procedures to applicable programs.

Provides guidance to all users through the development of policies, procedures, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and electronic tracking systems; as well as dissemination of information related to the appropriate program. Publishes guidance to enhance and simplify completion and submission of related actions.

Provides supervision of subordinate staff through the planning, assignment, and review of work; granting of leave; providing recommendation of training requirements, performance standards, and ratings; and effecting minor disciplinary actions such as warnings and reprimands.

Responsible for the overall training and professional development of subordinates.

Excellent communication and customer service skills.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.
Join Vanta's People team as a People Operations Specialist and help scale the foundation that enables every Vanta'n to do their best work - securely, efficiently and with confidence.
In this role, you'll be at the heart of our People operations: ensuring data integrity, streamlining workflows through automation, and partnering cross-functionally to improve both our internal processes and the broader employee experience. You'll work closely with our Manager, People Operations, and collaborate alongside our People Ops Generalists to keep our programs running smoothly and with intention.
This is an ideal opportunity for someone who is systems-minded, energized by fast-paced environments, and excited to grow at the intersection of People Ops and technology.

s.h: What you’ll do as a People Operations Specialist at Vanta
s.t:
System Administration: Maintain our core HR systems (e.g., HRIS, performance platforms, onboarding tools, etc.).
Data Integrity & Reporting: Own the accuracy, confidentiality, and integrity of employee data.
Automation & Workflow Optimization: Identify manual processes and proactively build scalable solutions using automation and integrations across tools. Translate complex business needs into efficient, repeatable processes.
Employee Lifecycle Administration: Process key employment changes — including new hires, terminations, promotions, transfers, etc — ensuring timely and accurate updates across People systems and cross-functional stakeholders.
US Immigration Administration: Serve as the day-to-day owner of US visa processes, including H-1B transfers, PERM applications, and other employment-based immigration filings — partnering closely with external and internal counsel and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure timely, compliant execution.
Policy & Documentation Ownership: Maintain and update People policies, process documentation, and system configurations to ensure accuracy and accessibility. Serve as a day-to-day resource for People systems questions and troubleshooting across our HR tech stack.
Compliance & Audits: Ensure system configurations and data meet compliance requirements (e.g., I-9s, security and compensation audits, employment verifications). Lead audit data pulls and documentation support.
Teammate Experience: Serve as a resource to employees through our ticketing system — answering questions and resolving issues related to HR systems, data updates, and process flows with clarity and care.

s.h: How to be successful in this role
s.t:
2-3 years’ People Ops experience in a high growth, fast-paced environment
Strong interest in HR systems, data, and operations, with prior experience working in HRIS or related systems (e.g., HiBob, Workday, Ashby, Culture Amp, etc.)
Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of data integrity
Ability to build scalable systems and automate repetitive processes using tools and integrations
Able to navigate ambiguity and shifting priorities with a bias for action – bringing structure and clarity to issues that don’t come with a playbook
Comfortable managing sensitive data with a high degree of discretion and confidentiality
Strong problem-solving skills, operational rigor, and project management chops
Clear, effective written and verbal communication — able to collaborate across teams
Experience or openness towards building with AI
Proficiency with G-Suite, Slack, Zoom, and general aptitude for learning new software quickly
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.
Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.
About Vanta
We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation.

Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged.
Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

The United States Space Force (USSF) Civilian Talent Management Office (CTMO) at Joint Base San Antonio, Texas is searching for Human Resources Information Systems Specialist (NH-0201-03, GS 12/13 equivalent). Description: As a Human Resources Specialist for the U.S.

Space Force, you will serve as a technical expert and data innovator at the heart of the Civilian Talent Management Office, shaping how the service builds its elite workforce.

In this dynamic role, you will lead challenging projects to design, analyze, and automate critical human capital processes by harnessing the power of advanced data systems like PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

By transforming raw HR data into actionable intelligence, you will create sophisticated reports, deliver high-impact briefings to senior Space Force leaders, and develop innovative solutions to complex organizational challenges, ensuring that the USSF can recruit, hire, and retain the nation's top talent.

If you are a proactive problem-solver with a passion for data and a drive to build the workforce of the future, apply today to make your mark on the newest branch of the armed forces.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned and proactive Human Resources data expert with a proven mastery of federal HR information systems, particularly PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

This individual possesses an innate ability to not only extract and manipulate complex datasets but also to conduct deep-dive analyses, turning raw data into actionable intelligence and strategic recommendations for senior leadership.

As a natural problem-solver and leader, they are adept at independently managing projects, developing automated solutions for HR processes, and mentoring junior team members.

Their exceptional communication skills allow them to translate highly technical information into clear, compelling briefings and to build strong collaborative relationships across various DAF, Field Command, and installation organizations.

Ultimately, this professional is a forward-thinking innovator who combines deep knowledge of federal HR principles with advanced technical skill to drive data-centric decision-making and enhance the operational effectiveness of the U.S. Space Force. Key Skills and Abilities: 1.

Knowledge of a wide range of federal Human Resources (HR) laws, executive orders, regulations, policies, directives, instructions, and concepts governing HR functions. 2.

About Blackthorn
Blackthorn turns any organization's Salesforce® CRM into event planning software powered by their connected data. We're a growing, distributed team with teammates across the globe, and we build Salesforce-native tools that help teams create events, engage attendees, process payments, and measure success — all without leaving their CRM.

Our customers range from tiny nonprofits to global corporations, and our products are known for going live in hours, not weeks. We believe the best enterprise software should feel as intuitive as the apps you use every day.
Why our work matters
Most event management tools force teams to juggle disconnected systems, wrestle with flimsy integrations, and spend more time syncing data than planning events.

We're building the alternative: a connected platform inside Salesforce that gives organizations richer analytics to prove event ROI, better attendee experiences through personalization and automation, and the flexibility to fit any workflow.

Every feature we ship helps our customers spend less time on logistics and more time on the events themselves.
What the job will bring you

About Wolt
At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.
Wolt’s Courier Employment team is building something that doesn’t really exist yet — a cross-country infrastructure for employed courier operations across multiple geographies. We sit at the intersection of operations, people, legal, and compliance, and we’re doing it largely from scratch.
The function currently spans three countries (Finland, Germany, Croatia), each at a different stage of maturity and with different legal frameworks. Courier employment is managed in all these countries by a functional team handling strategy, structure and resources, and country-level teams focused on execution and operational excellence from the ground up.
We operate in a fast-moving environment with a high degree of uncertainty — regulatory, operational, and structural. If you’re energised by the possibilities and want to be the person who builds the playbook, this might be the right role for you.

Croatia doesn't have an independent Courier HR operating model yet. It has support from the general employee HR team, great people working hard, manual workarounds, and a scale-up landing in the next few months that the current setup wasn't built to absorb. This role exists to establish Courier HR expertise within the function and build the processes needed while running the team's day-to-day HR operations.
As Courier HR Senior Specialist in Croatia, you'll own the full employee lifecycle for a fast-growing courier workforce: onboarding, contracts, documentation, leave, and the HR side of a workforce that includes couriers relocating from abroad. This includes tracking of work permits and other integration and compliance related matters.
You'll be supported by the function’s core team and leadership and work closely with your Courier HR Lead, the Workforce Ops team, Legal, and the sourcing agencies bringing couriers in. You'll be the most senior Courier HR operator on the ground in Croatia day-to-day — which means you'll be trusted to make independent decisions and participate actively in building foundations and standards that will apply across all markets.
What you'll be doing
Employee lifecycle execution at scale
Own onboarding, contracts, documentation, and leave administration for Croatia's employed couriers, including the operational HR side of relocating couriers from abroad (documentation, work permit tracking, compliance).
Delegating and syncing with a Tier 1 HR team that handles standard inbound tickets and manual entry.
Build and maintain accurate employee records across HR systems as the courier base scales.
Handle the volume and pace of onboarding waves without letting quality or compliance slip.
Make the judgment calls on ambiguous or non-standard cases that come up, escalating appropriately to your Courier HR Lead or Legal.
Process and SOP creation
Create SOPs, checklists, and documentation in collaboration with the functional Process & Systems Senior Specialist based on cross-market standards and calibrated to local requirements.
Identify where the current setup will break under the incoming scale-up, then plan and build for it before it breaks.
Partner with the Process & Systems Senior Specialist on anything that should become a cross-country standard rather than a local fix.
Cross-functional coordination
Act as the day-to-day HR point of contact for the sourcing agencies bringing couriers into Croatia, ensuring HR-side obligations (documentation, onboarding timing, permits) are met on time.
Work with Workforce Ops to keep HR and operational onboarding in sync as waves of new couriers arrive.
Flag structural risks early and initiate appropriate action in collaboration with your Lead and functional colleagues.
Our humble expectations
There’s no single background that defines this role — but the people who do well here tend to combine sharp analytical thinking with genuine operational curiosity. Some things that matter:
3+ years of experience in HR operations, people operations, or workforce administration — ideally somewhere that involved real scale, strict deadlines, or a workforce with cross-border or compliance complexity.
Experience working with foreign worker documentation, work permits, residence permits, or employment compliance processes.
A genuine ability to operate without a finished playbook. If "there's no process for this yet" makes you anxious rather than interested, this isn't the right role.
High attention to detail that holds up under volume and pressure — the documentation has legal weight, and the standard shouldn’t drop with rapidly increasing volume.
Good judgment about what to decide yourself and what to escalate. This role only works if you can be trusted with ambiguity — and trusted to know your own limits within it.
Fluency in Croatian (C1-C2) and professional level in English (B2-C2) are a requirement. Given the courier population arriving from abroad, comfort working through language and documentation barriers is a real asset — additional languages (Spanish, for instance) are a plus but not requirement.
Ability to work in a hybrid model from our Zagreb office (4 office days, Wednesday optional work-from-home day).

Most HR operations roles ask you to run a process well. This one asks you to build the process while running it, for a workforce that's about to grow faster than the current setup was designed for, in a market where the team is small and knowledge is yet to be mapped to documentation. You will work with a team of experts in multiple countries, giving you a unique chance to influence our strategies, standards and ways of working while constantly learning something new.
If it sounds like the kind of challenge you would enjoy solving, and if you are inspired by the potential of directly impacting the experience of hard working individuals establishing themselves in a new country, this will be a great opportunity for you.
Please note that this is a fixed-term contract until Dec 31st 2026, with a possibility to extend to a permanent contract. We’re expecting you to be able to start working with us during August-early September.

Directs and oversees personnel responsible for privileged administration of enterprise human resources systems, security administration, user access management, and production data maintenance activities.

Exercises delegated supervisory and managerial authority over subordinate supervisors and staff including planning and assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, interviewing and selecting employees, approving leave and administrative actions, resolving employee issues, identifying training needs, and ensuring accomplishment of organizational objectives.

Are you an experienced People Operations Specialist with a genuine interest and passion toward the operations side of HR? Do you want to be part of building and scaling our People Operations across the Nordics (Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Norway), with the autonomy to shape how we work while backed by a truly global People team? This is a hands-on role with plenty of room to improve and modernize our processes — if this sounds like you, then we’d love to chat!
Role Background
The People team at RELEX currently consists of 50 professionals located in several countries globally, the majority in Helsinki. To reach our growth plans and to ensure we serve our RELEXians to the best possible level, we are now looking for a full-time People Operations Specialist to join our People team in Helsinki, Finland or Stockholm, Sweden and take care of our Nordics region.
As our People Operations Specialist, you’ll be working at the very heart of our People Team, working to support and partner with our countries and functions in a highly engaged environment.

You are the first point of contact in HR matters and will be supporting the entire employee lifecycle for our colleagues mainly in Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Norway, from the very moment they onboard. You take care of HR data management, and you are also the main payroll partner for our external payroll vendor.
This is a great opportunity for someone with a “let’s get this done” mindset, looking to work in a fast-paced and developing environment, who likes to both co-create & work autonomously, enjoys a multicultural work environment and wants to make an impact.
What you'll be doing
Full employee life cycle support, from onboarding to offboarding and everything in between.
Supporting our team leads and colleagues with all their people-related topics, as e.g. time-off, benefits, compensation and others.
Responsible for Payroll input preparation in cooperation with our external payroll vendor.
HR system (Workday) updates and associated employee data quality management.
Writing and maintaining people policies, team lead guides and training sessions.
Handling employee escalation cases together with the support of your senior colleagues.

s.h: What you'll bring to the table
s.t:
You have a solid background of People Operations experience in the Nordics (focus countries Finland/Sweden, ideally also Norway and Denmark), preferably also in a multi-country, global environment.
You have previously worked closely with HR systems, people policies (creation and development), as well as compensation and benefits related topics.
You have hands-on experience with the payroll cycle.
You have a strong understanding of all core people processes, with a view of what works and what doesn’t.
You enjoy taking responsibility and solving problems proactively.
Excellent organizational skills and can-do attitude combined with networking skills, assertiveness, and the willingness to take initiative.
Strong problem-solving and communication skills
Full working fluency in English

You’ll be supported and given the space to thrive. We offer meaningful work, flexibility, and a culture that backs you to share your voice and be authentic.
An international career and learning opportunities
A rapidly growing and financially robust software company with exciting opportunities for career growth, also in the future

s.t:
Flexibility in how and where you work
Room to thrive in a fast-growing global company with a good market position
Practical benefits that support work, family, wellness, and everyday life
Annual leave
Diverse, inclusive, and supportive work culture
Work that meaningfully reduces waste and improves sustainability
Ownership, autonomy and flat hierarchies
Two paid volunteering days each year
We are a global community of different cultures, voices, and experiences. We celebrate what makes us unique and connect through what we share, in an authentic and safe environment. Together we shape the future, and each other.

Personalreferent – Recruiting & Neukundengewinnung (m/w/d)
Du bist im Vertrieb zuhause – und merkst langsam, dass dir etwas fehlt. Vielleicht eine Provision, die nicht bei einem festgelegten Wert endet. Vielleicht ein Produkt, hinter dem du wirklich stehst. Oder einfach der Punkt, an dem der Kunde nach der Unterschrift an jemand anderen übergeben wird und du nie erfährst, ob dein Versprechen gehalten hat.
Bei uns läuft das anders: Du gewinnst den Kunden
und lieferst danach selbst ab. Du berätst Unternehmen zu ihren Recruiting-Problemen, verkaufst die Lösung – und setzt sie anschließend eigenverantwortlich um. Ein Ansprechpartner, ein Verantwortlicher, ein Ergebnis.
Wir sind eine wachsende Recruiting-Beratung mitten in der Bielefelder Innenstadt. Wir helfen Unternehmen dabei, ihre Arbeitgebermarke sichtbar zu machen und planbar qualifizierte Mitarbeiter zu gewinnen – mit datenbasiertem Recruiting statt Bauchgefühl. Der Markt dafür wächst jedes Jahr weiter, weil Fachkräftemangel und demografischer Wandel nicht kleiner werden.
Was für dich drin ist
Fixgehalt plus ungedeckelter Bonus – kein Deckel, keine gestaffelten Bremsen. Was du holst, bekommst du.
Unbefristete Festanstellung – wir bauen langfristig auf dich, in einer Branche, die stabil wächst.
Zweites Standbein: Recruiting-Know-how – du lernst nicht nur zu verkaufen, sondern auch zu liefern. Das Doppelprofil aus Vertrieb und Recruiting ist im Markt aktuell das gefragteste überhaupt. Entwicklungspfad: Sales Consultant → Senior Consultant.
Strukturiertes Onboarding & echtes Coaching – Schulungen in Beratung, Vertrieb und Recruiting, dazu regelmäßige Feedback-Sessions statt einmaliger Einarbeitung.
Arbeitsplatz ohne Kompromisse – höhenverstellbare Tische, Herman-Miller-Stühle, Apple-Technik (MacBook Air/Pro, iMac), Büro in der Bielefelder Innenstadt.
Premium-Fitnessvertrag im Studio deiner Wahl.
Versorgung im Office – Faema-E61-Siebträger mit Julius-Meinl-Kaffee, gute Tees und flexibles Lunch-System über Meyer Menü.
Kurze Wege – direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung, kollegiale und leistungsorientierte Atmosphäre. Deine Ideen landen nicht in einer Schublade.
Dein Tag bei uns
Du gewinnst die Projekte
Du sprichst potenzielle Neukunden aktiv an – telefonisch, per Video-Call und über Direktansprache – und weckst Interesse an unseren digitalen Recruiting-Lösungen.
Du analysierst, woran das Recruiting im jeweiligen Unternehmen hakt, benennst den konkreten Handlungsbedarf und entwickelst daraus eine passende Strategie.
Du präsentierst deine Lösung und führst den Prozess bis zum Abschluss.
Du setzt sie um
Nach der Unterschrift steuerst du das Projekt eigenständig weiter – von der Kampagnenplanung bis zur besetzten Stelle.
Du koordinierst eingehende Bewerbungen, führst die Vorqualifizierung und sorgst dafür, dass Kandidaten einen professionellen Eindruck von deinem Kunden bekommen.
Dein Fundament
Du pflegst deine Aktivitäten sauber im CRM, behältst deine Pipeline im Blick und arbeitest zielgerichtet auf deine KPIs hin.
Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing und Geschäftsführung zusammen und bringst eigene Ideen zur Prozessverbesserung ein.
Das solltest du mitbringen
Vertriebserfahrung – ob Telefonvertrieb, Außendienst, Einzelhandel, Fitness- oder Versicherungsbranche: Wenn du weißt, wie sich ein "Nein" anfühlt und wie man trotzdem weitermacht, passt das.
Beratungsverständnis – du erkennst Potenziale, stellst die richtigen Fragen und bringst Lösungen strukturiert rüber.
Menschenkenntnis – du verstehst die Perspektive des Unternehmens genauso wie die des Bewerbers.
Eigeninitiative und Leistungswille – du arbeitest selbstständig und willst überdurchschnittliche Ergebnisse, nicht durchschnittliche.
Recruiting-Vorerfahrung ist ein Plus, kein Muss. Das Handwerk bringen wir dir bei. Uns interessiert weniger dein Lebenslauf als das, was du daraus machen willst.
So geht es weiter
Bewerben in 2 Minuten – ohne Anschreiben, dein Lebenslauf reicht.
Kurzes Kennenlern-Telefonat – wir melden uns innerhalb weniger Tage.
Persönliches Gespräch in unserem Office in der Bielefelder Innenstadt.
Nimm deinen Erfolg JETZT selbst in die Hand – wir freuen uns auf dich!

Job Description

People Operations is the operational engine of the People function at Cint.
Our mission is to build a scalable, intelligent and employee-centric operating model that enables the business to grow without increasing complexity. We achieve this by combining exceptional operational excellence with technology, automation and AI.
The way companies operate is changing rapidly. AI is transforming how work gets done, employees expect consumer-grade experiences, and global businesses need operations that scale without adding complexity. Most People Operations functions are still built for yesterday's world. We intend to build one for tomorrow.
This role will lead that transformation.
You will work closely with People Technology, Employee Relations, People Partners, Talent Teams, Total Rewards, Payroll, IT and Legal. You'll lead the evolution of our global People Operations function, combining operational excellence, technology, automation and AI to build a service that is fast, intelligent and ready for the future.

Build the People Operations function of the future: Redesign how People Operations works globally, creating an operating model that is simple, scalable and built to support a fast-growing international business.
Lead with technology, not manual work: Continuously identify opportunities to automate, simplify and redesign processes using AI, workflows and modern HR technology. If a process requires unnecessary manual effort, you'll challenge it.
Deliver service people actually love: Create an employee and manager experience that is intuitive, responsive and effortless. Great service isn't just about resolving tickets—it's about making support almost invisible.
Turn operations into a competitive advantage: Own service delivery globally through clear governance, operational controls and meaningful performance metrics that drive continuous improvement.
Lead and inspire a high-performing global team: Build a culture of accountability, ownership and innovation where people are empowered to solve problems, improve processes and think beyond today's way of working.
Partner across the business: Work closely with HR, People Technology, IT, Finance, Legal and business leaders to solve operational challenges, deliver complex initiatives and create joined-up employee experiences.
Use data, but apply judgement: Leverage operational metrics and workforce insights to identify trends, predict risks and make better decisions—while recognising that dashboards never replace critical thinking.
Own complexity so others don't have to: Act as the senior escalation point for complex People Operations matters, balancing compliance, employee experience and business priorities with sound judgement.
Build for scale before it's needed: Design resilient operations that support organisational growth, new markets and changing business needs without constantly adding more people or processes.
Never stop improving: Constantly ask why things are done a certain way, challenge existing assumptions and build a culture where continuous improvement is simply how work gets done.

We're looking for a high-ownership People Business Partner to support our Product and Design organizations at Gusto. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable analyzing data to surface a team health trend, running a clean reorg end-to-end, and building a lightweight process that makes a program actually land. Gusto's People team is growing and scaling with the company! As our business scales and becomes more complex, and as we add hundreds of new Gusties each year, we need to ensure that our strategies for engagement with our employees are positive, engaging, values-driven and compliant.

Build trusted partnerships with Product Management and Product Design leaders - understanding what's happening in their teams, surfacing friction early, and navigating performance management, promotions, leveling, and employee relations matters with good judgment.
Synthesize People data - engagement survey, performance cycles, attrition signals, headcount trends - into clear, actionable reads for Product and Design leaders before they have to ask.
Support and operationalize core talent programs including performance cycles, calibration discussions, promotion processes, and manager enablement.
Reinforce high performance standards, accountability, and clarity around expectations, feedback, and growth across Product Management and Product Design.
Serve as the liaison between Product & Design and Gusto's broader People team (Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, L&D, People Ops), translating company-wide programs into what they mean for product and design orgs - and surfacing that context back to the center.

Track record of executing complex People initiatives end-to-end - org changes, performance cycles, talent calibrations - owning the process and outcome, not just the advisory role.
High-Ownership Executor: Blends high-trust business partnership with hands-on execution - earns credibility through follow-through, not decks, and owns the details, dependencies, and timeline without being pushed.
Program Partner and COE Integrator: Acts as the connective tissue between Product Management, Product Design, and the wider People team, staying accountable for outcomes while pulling in the right COE capability - and builds those relationships proactively.
Builder & AI-Native: Builds lightweight, scalable People processes and reaches for AI to do it, without waiting for a perfect framework. Knows when to iterate on what AI gives them and when to keep the human in the loop.
High Judgment, Low Bureaucracy: Applies People principles without creating unnecessary process - assesses risk and nuance quickly, and knows when a situation needs a scalable solution versus a good answer now.
Comfortable Navigating Ambiguity and Driving Transformation: Operates effectively without perfect information, brings structure to complexity, and leads through change - ideally at Gusto-scale or larger.

Définition de la fonction et mission
Le/la HR Generalist assure le support opérationnel RH au quotidien pour tous les salariés du site de Montreux, sous la supervision du HR Manager.

Il/elle est le point de contact de proximité des collaborateurs pour l'ensemble du cycle RH : recrutement, onboarding/offboarding, administration du personnel, gestion de la relation employé et organisation d'événements internes.

Sa mission est de garantir la fiabilité et la fluidité des processus RH, tout en contribuant aux initiatives d'engagement, de formation et de performance définies par l-équipe RH.

* Support HR & Partenariat Accompagner le HR Manager et les équipes de direction en fournissant un support RH au quotidien, aligné sur les besoins du business.
* Contribuer à l'élaboration des initiatives de recrutement, de fidélisation et d'engagement des collaborateurs.
* Recrutement et Intégration Accompagner les managers dans la conduite des processus de recrutement.
* Assurer les tâches courantes de recrutement : publication des offres d'emploi, présélection des candidats, coordination des entretiens et préparation des offres.
* Garantir une expérience d'intégration réussie, incluant la préparation du welcome kit et des programmes d'induction.
* Gérer les démarches administratives liées à l'intégration et au départ des collaborateurs, en assurant des transitions fluides.
* Administration du Personnel et Conformité Tenir à jour les dossiers du personnel (contrats, avenants, données personnelles), en conformité avec le droit du travail suisse et le RGPD.
* Veiller au respect des lois du travail et des politiques de l'entreprise, notamment en matière de documentation, de sécurité et d'exigences légales ; remonter les problématiques au HR Manager si nécessaire.
* Soutenir le HR Manager lors des audits et suivre les évolutions réglementaires.
* Contribuer à la préparation des rapports et des analyses RH afin d'appuyer la prise de décision.
* Collaborer étroitement avec les Spécialistes Payroll et Gestion des Temps pour garantir un suivi précis et dans les délais de la paie et des présences.
* Relations et Engagement des Collaborateurs Entretenir des relations solides avec les collaborateurs en étant leur premier point de contact pour toute question ou préoccupation du quotidien.
* Promouvoir une culture d'entreprise ouverte et inclusive, alignée sur les valeurs de la société.
* Participer à la mise en œuvre d'initiatives visant à renforcer l'engagement, le moral et le bien-être des collaborateurs.
* Organiser et coordonner les événements internes, incluant les activités de team-building, journées à thème et célébrations.
* Gestion de la Performance et Développement des Compétences Contribuer au suivi des plans de développement de carrière des collaborateurs à haut potentiel.
* Soutenir le déploiement de programmes de formation adaptés, en coordination avec le HR Manager et la CLP Academy.
* Gérer l'ensemble des aspects administratifs liés aux formations.
* Excellence Opérationnelle RH Veiller à ce que les processus RH soient efficaces et conformes aux objectifs de l'organisation.
* Maintenir les systèmes RH à jour, en garantissant l'exactitude des données et la confidentialité.
* Compiler les indicateurs RH et fournir au HR Manager des analyses exploitables.
* Alignement Culturel et Valeurs Incarner les valeurs de Clinique La Prairie en les intégrant au quotidien, en favorisant une culture d'excellence, de collaboration et de respect.
* Porter des initiatives favorisant l'inclusion, la diversité et une culture d'entreprise positive.
* Contribuer aux programmes renforçant la mission, la vision et les valeurs de l'entreprise.

* CFC ou formation commerciale équivalente ; Brevet fédéral de spécialiste RH ou en cours d'obtention fortement apprécié
* 4 à 6 ans d'expérience dans un rôle RH généraliste, idéalement dans l'hôtellerie, le luxe, la santé/wellness ou un environnement de service similaire

* Expérience en administration du personnel : maîtrise des processus liés à l'ensemble du cycle de vie du collaborateur (contrats, avenants, gestion des dossiers du personnel, suivi des absences et congés), avec une bonne connaissance du droit du travail suisse et une rigueur dans la conformité documentaire et légale (RGPD/LPD).
* Maîtrise des outils bureautiques (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) et idéalement d'un SIRH (HRIS).
* Proactif-ve et curieux-se : anticipe les besoins des équipes plutôt que d'attendre les sollicitations, propose des améliorations et cherche à comprendre le fonctionnement des différents départements pour mieux les accompagner.
* Une appétence pour le recrutement : à l'aise dans l'évaluation des candidats, aime le contact humain et s'intéresse aux techniques de sourcing et d'entretien pour contribuer activement aux recrutements de l'établissement.
* Français et anglais courants
* Sens de la confidentialité, rigueur administrative, excellent relationnel et capacité à travailler en équipe sous la supervision du HR Manager.

Sr. People Operations Manager
Role Description
You will own the infrastructure, systems, and data layer that keeps MagicSchool 's People function running cleanly at scale - executing a Year 1 project portfolio (PEO transition, EOR setup, contingent workforce vendor, unified HR data architecture) while building the steady-state processes that make the employee experience reliable and the People team's work credible.

In this role, you will be responsible for driving towards the following outcomes:
People Systems & Data Infrastructure: Own HRIS, PEO, and Lattice end-to-end - configuration, vendor relationships, and system hygiene - and build the unified data layer connecting HRIS, payroll, and equity administration so headcount, comp, and employment data have a single source of truth leadership can use with confidence.
Process Architecture & Lifecycle Design: Design and maintain employee lifecycle workflows from onboarding through exit, owning the templates and documentation that make those processes scalable and reduce rework as the company grows.
PEO & Contingent Workforce Transition: Project-manage the transition off MagicSchool 's current PEO (benefits, payroll continuity, vendor selection) and stand up a new contingent workforce vendor for contractor administration and compliance, owning both timelines end to end.
IT Onboarding/Offboarding & EOR Administration: Own end-to-end IT provisioning/deprovisioning in partnership with IT, and manage the Employer of Record relationship for Canadian employees, ensuring legal and operational requirements are met throughout.

To be successful in this role, you'll bring the following skills and competencies:
HR Data Architecture Fluency: You think in terms of source-of-truth, data hygiene, and system integrations, and can build models, write formulas, and create reports people actually use.
Ownership-Oriented Execution: You build the playbook rather than wait for one — flagging blockers early, closing loops without being chased, and treating this as an ownership role rather than a support role.
Experience
Required: 5-8 years in HR operations, people operations, or related roles, with meaningful time spent on systems implementation and operational infrastructure.
Required: Proven track record leading a PEO transition, HRIS implementation, or comparable infrastructure project.
Preferred (Nice-to-Have): Experience with EOR and/or contingent workforce management.

As our Working Student in HR Operations, you'll be right in the middle of the action keeping our HR function running smoothly, helping our HR team stay one step ahead as we scale, from coordinating on-boarding to preparing welcome merchandise to keeping our HRIS up to date.
This role goes beyond routine admin. We are looking for someone flexible and reliable who is comfortable filling in the gaps, spotting what needs attention, and supporting the team wherever the workload calls for it.

Onboarding Coordination: You help coordinate the on boarding processes for our new hires, scheduling, documentation, system access, preparing the welcome merchandise and making sure everything is ready before their first day.
HRIS Maintenance: You assist in keeping our HRIS accurate and up to date, whether through your regular monthly update or as changes come in throughout the month.
Employee Inquiries: You act as a first point of contact for everyday employee questions, answering what you can and routing anything more complex to the right person on the team.
General HR Support: You fill in the little gaps across HR operations, whatever the team needs that week, helping keep things running without anything falling through the cracks.
You are currently enrolled as a student (Bachelor's or Master's), ideally in HR, business administration, psychology, or a related field.
You are flexible and comfortable switching between different types of tasks day to day.
You have an ownership mentality and ready to take on tasks as they come.
You have a strong eye for detail, especially when it comes to data accuracy and confidentiality.
You are organized and reliable, and enjoy jumping in wherever help is needed.
You are proficient in Leapsome (highly welcome)
You are fluent in German and English, both spoken and written.
Prior experience in HR, recruiting, or an administrative operations are required.
Why TYTAN?
Build technology with real operational impact: Develop autonomous defence systems designed to protect lives and strengthen Europe’s security
Shape scalable defence capabilities: Work on solutions built for mass deployment, cost efficiency, resilience, and reliable production at scale
Contribute to networked air defence: Help integrate our systems into multi-layered defence architectures alongside sensors, command systems, and effectors
Develop for real-world operations: Build capabilities together with end users and improve them continuously based on direct operational feedback
Move fast and take ownership: Work in a focused, high-performance team where decisions are made quickly and individual contributions have immediate impact
Define a new generation of defence technology: Join early and help shape the products, engineering standards, culture, and direction of a fast-growing deep-tech company
Work with an international mission-driven team: Collaborate with experienced specialists united by the goal of creating sovereign and effective security capabilities for Europe

Monthly allowances: €68/month in flexible benefits including lunch discounts and EGYM Wellpass or shopping credit
Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us
Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team
Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together
Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands
Flexibility : Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.
Role Purpose
Our clinics are where Neko shows up most tangibly – for our members and for our teams. Nowhere carries more of that than the UK: currently our largest clinical market, and the clearest test of whether our people practices hold up under real growth. What members experience in clinic is downstream of how those teams are built and led.
This role operates across two teams: a cross-functional People team that supports UK clinics locally, and Neko's global People Partner team, focused on clinics and operations worldwide – together built to deliver one people agenda that holds up locally and at scale.

As UK Lead, this role owns the full people strategy behind how the UK scales: what the organisation looks like, how clinic teams are shaped and staffed, how people are led, developed, and rewarded, and what it feels like to work here. It also carries the embedded, day-to-day work of keeping clinics running well today.

Both, at the same time, and neither at arm's length.

s.h: What you'll do in the first 6-12 Months
s.t:
Own the clinical people agenda for the UK
Be the day-to-day People partner across UK clinical leadership – senior operations and medical leaders through to frontline clinic managers – owning workforce planning, organisational design, and talent decisions for the clinical population
Sit at the table with UK clinical leadership as the voice of the people agenda
Support the development and internal mobility routes that let clinical talent grow – into deeper expertise, wider scope, or leadership
Work as part of a cross-functional local People team – alongside TA, Rewards, Growth, and People Ops partners – to deliver one joined-up agenda for UK clinics
Be embedded in clinics
Spend real time in clinics to understand how work actually happens – not just what's written down
Build trust with clinic teams by showing up consistently, listening carefully, and following through
Stay close to what members experience in clinic, and read it as signal about how the team is resourced, structured, and led
Bring sound judgement and discretion to the most sensitive people matters on the clinical floor
Help clinic leaders lead well
Coach leaders through hiring, performance, and the conversations that are hard but important
Build the leadership capability and multi-way feedback culture that keep employee relations issues from piling up – and support teams and leaders through the ones that do
Support first-time clinic managers as they build confidence, capability, and steady leadership habits
Turn central People programmes into clinic-ready practice, and call out where a centralised approach misses frontline reality
Data-informed, judgement-led, moving at the pace of the business
Use staffing patterns, clinical pipeline data, and on-the-ground signal to shape workforce decisions ahead of need
Put data and AI to work in how the People agenda actually runs – sharper decisions, less manual effort, and more time on the judgement calls and the highest-impact work
Spot strain, inconsistency, or risk early, and address it before it reaches a member – team strain usually shows up in the clinic room before it shows up in the data
Take change from decision to genuine adoption – bringing clinic teams with you, without pausing delivery to do it
Hold both hats: UK delivery and global clinical strategy
Operate as part of Neko's global People Partner team, and help drive its clinical strategy rather than just feed into it
Bring the UK's clinical reality into that team's agenda, so decisions made at scale hold up on the ground

8+ years as a senior People or HR Business Partner leader, supporting both senior levels of leadership and frontline leaders of larger teams
Experience holding a local delivery mandate and a genuine seat in broader, cross-market strategy at the same time
A track record of leading people change in fast-moving, scaling businesses – comfortable revisiting what you built six months ago because the business has moved

Working knowledge of UK employment law, with the judgement to know when to bring in specialist expertise
Based in London, and ready to spend regular time in clinics

You're comfortable being the systems administrator of SaaS platforms: owning permissions, workflows, and integrations, ideally across an HRIS/ATS/EOR stack (HiBob, Ashby, Remote) or a comparable set of business systems.
You've worked in a high-growth environment, ideally remote and across multiple geographies, and you're comfortable working async across EMEA time zones.
Any exposure to People Ops, HR systems, or UK employment practices is a genuine bonus, not a
requirement - we're hiring for the builder instinct first, and will coach the domain knowledge.
You’ll Thrive Here If You…
You're an Owner. You don't wait to be told the onboarding flow needs fixing, you notice the friction and you just fix it.
You're Fast. You'd rather ship a working automation this week and improve it next week than spend a month designing the perfect one.
You like Simple. Your default build is the one with the fewest moving parts, not the most impressive one.
You find Surprising in the unglamorous stuff. You get a kick out of turning "someone does this by hand every month" into something nobody thinks about again.
You're Human, even with agents. You know the systems you're building sit behind someone's first week at a new job, or a colleague's benefits question — you design for that person, not just for the workflow diagram.

The Senior HR Business Partner acts as a key strategic advisor to the Head of Human Resource for Singapore, translating business strategy — including new and emerging manpower requirements arising from the company's ongoing business pivot — into actionable workforce plans.

He/she proactively develops workforce plans, identifies capability and headcount gaps, advises management on employment compliance matters, and partners with business leaders to co-create people solutions that enable the organisation's evolving objectives.

The role works in close partnership with the Recruitment (Blue & White Collar) and HR Operations functions to ensure workforce plans and compliance requirements are translated into effective execution.

Workforce Planning & Organisation Design
Partners with the Head of HR and business/department leaders to translate business strategy — including new directions arising from the business pivot — into headcount and workforce plans (build, buy, borrow or redeploy).
Leads annual and ad-hoc workforce planning exercises, forecasting manpower demand against the current organisation structure.
Conducts capability and skills gap analyses against current and future business needs, and recommends closing strategies (reskilling, upskilling, hiring, restructuring).
Designs and proposes new roles, job families and reporting structures required to support emerging business lines.
HR Business Partnering & Advisory
Serves as the primary HR point of contact and trusted advisor to assigned business unit(s)/department heads on people-related matters.
Proactively analyses people data (attrition, vacancies, engagement survey results, exit interviews) to shape data-driven recommendations to management.
Solutions together with business leaders on new and emerging manpower requirements as the business pivots, translating ambiguous business needs into concrete HR plans.
Builds and maintains strong stakeholder relationships through regular business/operations reviews and consultation sessions.
Advises management and department heads on Singapore employment legislation, MOM regulations (including the work pass framework, Employment Act and Tripartite Guidelines) and related statutory obligations.
Partners with the HR Operations team to ensure HR policies, contracts and practices stay compliant with regulatory changes, escalating and closing gaps as needed.
Provides guidance on complex or sensitive employee relations matters, applying sound judgement within local legislative parameters.
Employment Compliance & Risk Advisory
Partners closely with the Recruitment team (blue & white collar) to translate workforce plans into hiring plans, prioritise critical roles and calibrate sourcing strategy for new manpower requirements.
Partners closely with the HR Operations team to ensure new organisation structures, role changes and headcount movements are accurately reflected in the HRIS, contracts and policies.
Acts as a key thought partner to the Head of HR, representing Singapore HR in relevant business and management forums as required.

* **Responsibility** for the entire employee life cycle, from onboarding to offboarding, including personnel administration, social insurance, payroll (including withholding taxes) and expenses, and close collaboration with our recruiting team
* **Advising, supporting and assisting** our employees and Team Leads with a wide range of HR-related matters
* **Central HR Controlling**
* **Actively driving forward and operationally implementing** our HR roadmap, contributing to HR projects and optimizing existing processes
* **Ensuring the transfer of knowledge** and the provision of training on HR processes and tools

* **Providing cover** for colleagues and supporting the Location Management and Corporate Services teams, including reception, telephone services and infrastructure
* **Ensuring compliance** with processes and procedures and reviewing their legal compliance, particularly in the areas of employment law, social insurance law, tax law, international regulations and the Swiss Data Protection Act; supporting the identification and monitoring of risks and preparing reports

\#GrowTogether - that is our credo! Do you enjoy the wide range of activities involved in the employee life cycle? As a passionate and empathetic HR professional, are you eager to accompany our company on its continued journey of internationalization and growth? As a proactive doer with high-quality standards, are you energized by a dynamic working environment and keen not only to manage processes, but also to drive change?
In addition to sound HR expertise - including Swiss employment law, social insurance, payroll and, ideally, global mobility - you have strong numerical acumen and an analytical mindset. You are comfortable working with payroll data, HR controlling, reports and spreadsheets. Combined with your business acumen, strong communication skills and high degree of personal responsibility, you bring the following qualifications:

For this role, regular presence in our Lugano office is expected. Occasional travel to other adesso locations may also be required, typically once a month, primarily to Zurich or Bern.

Senior People Partner - London or Manchester - Hybrid
The Opportunity
At Inizio, we are a global team with a shared purpose: to reimagine health. We bring together specialist capabilities across advisory, medical, marketing, communications, engagement and biotech to help health and life sciences organisations solve complex challenges and create meaningful outcomes for clients, patients and communities.
As Inizio grows, our People & Culture team is helping the organisation become more connected, consistent and future-ready. We are building the leadership, capability and culture needed for the next stage of growth.
This is a great opportunity to join the Central Functions HR team at an important point in Inizio's journey. You will partner with leaders across the central group functions, helping them strengthen their teams, shape the future organisation and create the conditions for people to thrive.

Reporting to the Global Head of HR for Corporate Functions, the Senior People Partner will be a trusted partner to leaders across Inizio's central group functions. You will be about helping leaders make confident people decisions, strengthen capability and build teams that are ready for the future.
You will bring a blend of strategic thinking, practical judgement and stakeholder partnership, working with leaders who are at different stages of growth, change and maturity.
You will work with People Services and HR Centres of Expertise. This includes Talent Management, Reward, Talent Acquisition, Employee Relations, and People Solutions. You will connect enterprise People & Culture priorities to what leaders practically need daily.
You will play an important part in helping the central functions continue to evolve. It will support culture, leadership effectiveness, succession, engagement, organisation design, and the ongoing development of a proactive, commercially connected HR function.
Here's what you'll be doing
You will partner with leaders across IT, Finance, HR and other central group functions to build stronger teams, clearer ways of working and the capability needed for Inizio's next stage of growth.

Build trusted relationships with functional leaders, understanding their priorities, team dynamics and where they are on their growth and development journeys.
Help leaders shape the capability, culture and leadership behaviours their teams will need to thrive in a more connected Inizio.
Act as a coach and partner, offering thoughtful challenge, sound judgement and support on people, team and leadership priorities.
Work with Talent Management and Talent Development to make talent reviews, succession and development planning meaningful, practical and future-focused.
Partner with Talent Acquisition so hiring decisions strengthen both the capability and culture we are building across the central functions.
Collaborate with Total Rewards on fair, well-governed and commercially sensible reward decisions, including salary review, bonus, benchmarking and job architecture.
Use data, insight and employee feedback to help leaders understand what is working, where risks may be emerging and how to create the right conditions for people to perform.
Support organisation design and change activity where needed, with a focus on clarity, leader readiness, and a positive employee experience.
Embed Inizio-wide People and Culture processes and tools in a way that feels simple, useful and relevant for leaders.
Work across People Services,People Solutions Employee Relations, Legal and the HR Centres of Expertise to provide joined-up, proactive and value-adding HR support.
