Senior People Partner
📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 4 days WFH) | 💰 £60,000 - £70,000
Street Group is a fast moving B2B SaaS business - grown in Manchester but on a UK wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We’ve recently raised Series B funding, and are scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan - and we’re looking for a Senior People Partner to ensure we get there.
Over the past 6 years, our People team has designed, built, and implemented the people processes that have scaled Street Group from 30 - 230 people. But we know that systems that work at 150 people can break at 300 - and we want to get ahead of that.
This is an opportunity for someone who has been through that scaling journey before to have an oversized impact on a small but ambitious People team to become best in class.
If you know what can impact culture both positively and negatively as a company grows; have experience building systems that both set people up to do their best work AND that scale alongside the business; and embrace AI and the positive impact it can have on employee experience - we think you might do great work here.
Why this role exists now
Our People team is lean - and as we mature as a business, there’s limited capacity to ensure we’re constantly innovating and improving the mechanisms that enable people to do their best work. We have ambitious goals to achieve - now is the time to fine-tune our People function to ensure the business hits those goals.

In 2026, over half of the business told us they don't know what excellence looks like in their role, or how excellence is rewarded. This is the crux of this role; to build the systems, processes and reward that sets people up for success and ensure we reward and retain our best people.
Over the next 12-18 months, this will mean you'll be working with our Head of People and People Partner on initiatives that clarify excellence and reward - our internal levels framework, compensation & reward, embedding our excellence standard throughout the business, and coaching managers on a team by team basis to increase overall performance.

An experienced People Partner passionate about their craft; curious about how technology and innovation is changing the People landscape, and constantly looking for more impactful ways to support the business.
A commercial mindset - e.g. you measure your results on impact on business and team performance rather than work shipped.
An AI-native mindset: you treat AI as leverage and are keen to learn from our team, and share what’s been working for you - but understand the nuances of where AI can never replace genuine People Partnering.
The credibility and communication skills to bring busy managers on the journey with you.
Someone who makes the team better on purpose, not by accident: you share what you know and help develop the people around you.
Why you might not want to apply
We'd rather be honest up front, because this role won’t be for everyone.
If you want to move into people management. This is a senior IC role. You'll coach, share knowledge, and set standards, but you won't have direct reports. If a management title is what you're chasing now or in the imminent future, this isn’t the job for you.
If you haven't been through a similar scaling journey in SaaS businesses before. Our People team is home grown; we're specifically looking for the experience and knowledge that comes from having been there/done that before, and can prevent us from making common mistakes.
If AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. We love Claude Cowork, and have both built and used multiple other tools to improve and speed up our ways of working. We have a company-wide expectation that AI is utilised, so it will be a large part of this role.
If you want a role where you'll be spending a lot of time on pastoral employee interactions. This isn't going to be the main part of this role - you'll be spending most of your time building a culture of excellence.
If that list sounds like your kind of role, please apply and let us know why!
We recognise that women and people from underrepresented groups often apply for jobs only when they meet every single requirement listed. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application!
Who are Street Group?
We’re an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff. Most of us have personal experience of how painful moving can be, and Tom and Heather saw an opportunity to change this: utilising technology, as well as our incredibly talented team, to improve the industry for everyone.
Our products, Street.co.uk , Spectre & Cortex form a powerful trio, working harmoniously together to transform an agent’s job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills are essential as the position requires advising leadership, collaborating with internal and external stakeholders, and presenting information clearly and professionally.

The ideal candidate will also be highly organized, detail-oriented, capable of managing multiple priorities independently, and committed to delivering accurate, timely, and high-quality customer service.

* Du gestaltest Programme und Massnahmen rund um Führung, Zusammenarbeit, Kultur und Lernen mit und begleitest deren Umsetzung in den verschiedenen Bereichen der Finanzdirektion.
* Du begleitest organisationale Veränderungsprozesse und Teamentwicklungen und arbeitest dabei eng mit der HR-Beratung und weiteren beteiligten Fachstellen zusammen.
* Du konzipierst und moderierst Workshops und begleitest Teams und Führungskräfte methodisch und praxisnah durch Veränderungs- und Teamentwicklungsprozesse.
* Gemeinsam mit POE, der HR-Beratung und weiteren Fachstellen pilotierst du neue HR-Ansätze und Tools und begleitest deren Einführung in der Finanzdirektion.
* Du arbeitest in HR-Projekten mit, übernimmst bereichsübergreifende Aufgaben und stellst den Wissenstransfer innerhalb des HR Managements sicher.
### Dein Profil ###
* Du verfügst über einen Hochschulabschluss in HR Management, Personal- oder Organisationspsychologie oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
* Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung in einer vergleichbaren HR-Funktion sowie fundierte Erfahrung in der Begleitung von organisationalen Veränderungsprozessen und Teamentwicklungen mit.
* Leadership-Themen sind dir vertraut und du kennst verschiedene Ansätze rund um Führung, Zusammenarbeit und Organisation.
* Du denkst analytisch und konzeptionell, behältst auch bei komplexen Fragestellungen den Überblick und entwickelst praxistaugliche Lösungen.
* Du verfügst über eine hohe Beratungs- und Kommunikationskompetenz, moderierst sicher und schaffst es, unterschiedliche Anspruchsgruppen und Perspektiven einzubeziehen.
* Moderne HR-Instrumente und aktuelle HR-Trends sind dir vertraut und du interessierst dich für neue Ansätze.
### Unser Angebot ###
* Unser HR-Umfeld ist im Wandel. Ideal, wenn du gerne mitdenkst, mitgestaltest und Neues mit auf den Weg bringst.
* Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten und eine faire Entlöhnung sind bei uns selbstverständlich.
* Dein Arbeitsplatz liegt zentral und ist vom Zürcher HB in wenigen Minuten erreichbar.

About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The opportunity
Our People Partners are the eyes and ears of the organisation, embedded within their functional areas to be a sounding board for leaders, support managers and enable teams to thrive.

The People Partnering team operate on a strategic and tactical level, ensuring the people elements are in place for teams to effectively deliver their strategic objectives (think org design, upskilling, succession planning) whilst also offering one on one support, both structured and ad hoc, to those who need it most.
We're hiring an experienced, driven Senior People Partner to partner with our Chief Content Officer and the Content (Editorial, Legals, Credit, Distressed) team. Content is scaling fast across the UK and US, and we need a Senior People Partner who can move at pace, get to grips with what the team actually does, and hold their own with senior editorial and analytical leaders.
You'll be fully embedded in the Content team, with a real voice in leadership meetings, editorial rituals and off-sites. You'll know the leads, managers and rising talent well enough to catch the people issues long before they show up in engagement scores or exit interviews.
Every day is different, but here's an example of the kind of things you'll work on:
Strategic
Trusted advisor to your leaders : You'll be the first person Content leadership calls on anything people-related: the confidant, sounding board and thought partner they think alongside, not the person they update after the fact. That kind of trust is earned over time, through showing up and being willing to have the harder conversation when it matters.
Right hand person to the CCO: You know how he thinks about content and his organisation, and are confident acting as his proxy with his leaders to get them to where they need to be.
Locked in on what the team is trying to achieve : You know Content's goals, what its leaders and teams do. You bring solutions, not just observations, and follow them through to completion.
Fully embedded in your team : You're in the rituals, Slack channels and meetings that matter, so you've got a real read on how the team actually works. You cut through the noise to name the actual issue and get it resolved quickly and respectfully.
Catching things early : You join the dots across 1:1s, skips, engagement data and your own observations to surface people risks while they're still small and easy to fix. You coach leaders and managers to build the same instinct.
Org design : You advise on org shape, spot gaps and flag future risk areas. You make sure the right people are doing the right jobs at the right level as Content scales across regions and coverage.
Talent management : You know who the key talent is and you work with leaders to develop, stretch and reward them. You support leaders to identify their successors and build the development plans that get them ready. You work proactively with the Talent team on the pipelines for roles you can already see coming.
Learning & development : You spot where Content teams need to grow — editorial craft, analytical rigour, management skill, leadership development — and you lead the training that plugs the gap. A big part of that is upskilling managers to handle people issues themselves, early and well, rather than escalating them to the CCO. You diagnose early, source or build the right thing, and hold a bar for what impact should look like once it's landed.
Reward : You use solid data to inform our salary bands and keep compensation fair across the team, with D&I front of mind. You coach leaders and managers through promotion and salary reviews so decisions are thoughtful, equitable and defensible.
Performance : You help leaders and managers get the best out of their teams, surfacing blockers, coaching through them, and making sure feedback and training actually land. You hold a high bar yourself and help leaders hold one too.
Hands up for the bigger stuff : You take on projects that improve the People function as a whole, not just your patch. You scope them properly, influence stakeholders, manage the risks and dependencies, and ship on time.
Tactical
Employee Relations (ER) : Following UK employment law, navigating all employee relations within your business area, including but not limited to: managing Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs), resolving claims and grievances in line with policy, probation management, maternity and paternity cases, flexible working requests, conflict management and mediation, and any other employee-to-employee issue that comes up, both formally and informally.
Embedding people products : Working with the wider Partnering team to embed our people products and systems, delivering training, championing adoption and being the go-to person for questions. Delivering product feedback to the wider team on a regular basis.
Data : Pulling and analysing the right data to help managers and leaders make good calls and adding the context that turns numbers into something your leaders can actually use.
Wellbeing support : 1:1 support to employees when they need it, and making sure they know what mental and physical health support is on offer. Supporting managers through those conversations too.
Cultural ambassador : Working with leaders and managers to reinforce the right behaviours in teams. Being a role model yourself for our values and ways of working, especially as the London office grows.

s.h: This role will be a great fit if you
s.t:
Take real accountability for pushing back on leaders — not just flagging a concern and moving on, but staying with it until the right decision gets made.
Can confidently challenge executives and their most senior leaders when it matters, as a true partner rather than a service function.
Are properly curious about the business you support. You'll want to understand how Content produces its analysis, what makes a great desk, and what separates a good journalist from a world class one. You ask questions until you get to the real answer.
Are a strong influencer, able to help others look at things from different perspectives and understand the 'why' behind decisions. Comfortable pushing back on leaders and managers when needed, and know when to step back and let them make their own call.

We build AI that gives nurses more time for what matters. Your job is to bring that same mindset to our People function - cutting admin, removing friction, and creating an employee experience that sets the standard for how modern companies should operate.

Automate what shouldn’t be manual: Build a reliable source of truth and the workflows and AI agents around it - so documents, deadlines, data checks and repetitive admin run without human intervention.

This position is located within the Department of the Interior, Office of the Secretary (OS), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Policy, Management, and Budget (ASPMB), Office of Occupational Health and Safety, Workers Compensation Program (WCP).

At the full performance level (GS-12) the major duties of this position include, but are not limited to the following: Evaluate complex and potentially controversial workers' compensation claims by conducting thorough analysis of the circumstances surrounding the injury or illness, reviewing medical documentation, injury reports, witness statements, and any relevant employment or personnel records.

Utilize advanced knowledge of the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA), Office of Workers Compensation Program (OWCP) guidelines, and agency policies to determine the validity of claims, identify inconsistencies, and resolve discrepancies.

Manage complex workers' compensation claims from initial claim filing through case resolution and closure. Responsibilities include reviewing medical and factual evidence, analyzing investigative reports, and ensuring proper claim documentation in compliance with OWCP requirements.

The WCS provides case management oversight for sensitive, precedent-setting, or high-cost claims, coordinates with supervisors, safety officers, attorneys, labor relations officials, and OWCP staff to ensure timely adjudication and effective resolution.

Advise supervisors and managers on their responsibilities for injury reporting, medical documentation, workplace accommodations, and compliance with OWCP timeframes. Design, deliver, and evaluate training for supervisors, employees, and HR professionals to ensure proper understanding of FECA requirements and procedures.

Evaluate current case status and potential for alternate or light duty positions, retraining, and/or medical retirement works directly with DOL/OWCP and the Department to address complex cases.

Act as liaison between DOL/OWCP and claimant on complicated or particularly troublesome cases to ensure injured workers receive proper medical care and benefits. The Office of the Secretary has determined that the duties of this position are suitable for telework and may be allowed with supervisory approval.

Change the way the world travels
Join the GetYourGuide journey to connect people with unforgettable travel experiences around the world. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours.
Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step.
Team mission
Our People Services team powers the employee experience by facilitating change and helping navigate the moments that matter. We achieve this by providing efficient, knowledgeable, and reliable service to employees throughout their entire GetYourGuide journey, ensuring a compliant and empathetic approach.

To support us on this journey, we are seeking a dedicated People Operations Specialist to support our APAC employees. In this role, you'll be constantly learning and face new challenges daily, enabling you to enhance your HR skills and expertise across diverse areas of interest.

This role is based in Bangkok, and reports into our central People Operations team in Berlin, Germany.

Be the go-to People Operations contact for our APAC* employees, advising on local HR processes across the employee lifecycle - including onboarding/ offboarding, relocation and visa support, benefits administration, and coordination with local legal and tax advisors.
Champion operational efficiency by designing and maintaining sustainable, user-friendly, and effective HR processes that ensure local regulatory compliance and labor law requirements.
Act as a liaison between employees and leadership in APAC, and our central business teams in Germany, ensuring smooth communication and alignment.
Support low-performance management processes, including Performance Improvement Plans and resulting actions (i.e. separations, severance, offboarding) together with our centralized People Relations team.
Provide support in resolving employment legal matters related to misconduct investigations, employee grievances, crisis management, and other employment law matters.
Oversee APAC office operations focusing on Bangkok, including coordinating catering, F&B arrangements and managing office vendor relationships.
Collaborate with People Team stakeholders - such as People Partners, Payroll, People Relations, and People Systems - to deliver a seamless employee experience aligned with GetYourGuide's People strategy.
*our APAC offices are located in Bangkok, Hong Kong, Sydney, and Tokyo
Your toolkit
You are an HR manager or generalist with a university degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field.
You bring at least 4-5 years of experience in People Operations (HR) within a dynamic, fast-paced and international environment.
You are Fluent in English and Thai, both written and spoken, and comfortable communicating with stakeholders across different cultures and time zones.
In-depth knowledge of Thai labor law and collaboration with external lawyers; labor law and immigration knowledge for our other APAC regions is a big plus.
Experience with HRIS (preferably Workday), ticketing systems such as Jira (Service Desk) and Google Suite.
Exceptional interpersonal skills: a people-oriented individual who understands employee needs and can effectively guide diverse stakeholders.
You are highly organized, can manage priorities across multiple stakeholders and locations, and are comfortable reprioritizing in a high-velocity environment.
How we’ll make your career journey extraordinary
Annual personal growth budget and mentorship programs for continuous learning and development
Work from anywhere in the world for 30 days per year
A hybrid working approach with three days of in office collaboration (Mon, Tue, Thur) and two days of optional at home focus time.
Opportunities to collaborate and socialize with team members through quarterly team events and yearly company-wide events
Monthly transportation and fitness budget
Discounts for you, your friends, and family on GetYourGuide activities
Language reimbursement program
And more…

Sie verbinden operative HR-Kompetenz mit strategischem Weitblick? Bei der Aare Seeland mobil AG gestalten Sie die Personalarbeit, die Führungskultur und die Weiterentwicklung des Unternehmens aktiv mit.
Die Aare Seeland mobil AG ist eine bedeutende Anbieterin des öffentlichen Verkehrs und verbindet mit ihren Bahn- und Busangeboten Menschen und Regionen. Das regional stark verankerte Unternehmen verfügt über rund 245 Vollzeitstellen. Im Rahmen einer natürlichen Nachfolgeregelung infolge Pensionierung der bisherigen Stelleninhaberin suchen wir per 1. Januar 2027 oder nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte und erfahrene Persönlichkeit als
Leiter:in Human Resources - Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung
Sie verantworten gemeinsam mit Ihrem dreiköpfigen Team den gesamten HR Life Cycle – vom Eintritt bis zum Austritt – und stellen eine professionelle, verlässliche und dienstleistungsorientierte Personalarbeit sicher. Dabei verbinden Sie das operative Tagesgeschäft mit der konzeptionellen und strategischen Weiterentwicklung des HR-Bereichs.

Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung bringen Sie die personelle und organisatorische Sicht in unternehmensweite Fragestellungen ein und beraten den Direktor sowie die Führungskräfte auf Augenhöhe.

Sie entwickeln die Personalstrategie, die Rekrutierung, die Personalentwicklung und das Employer Branding weiter und begleiten Veränderungsprozesse mit Augenmass.

Als pragmatische Führungspersönlichkeit arbeiten Sie aktiv im Tagesgeschäft mit, übernehmen bei Bedarf selbst operative HR-Aufgaben und unterstützen Ihr Team dort, wo Ihre Mitarbeit gefragt ist. Gleichzeitig sorgen Sie für zeitgemässe HR-Instrumente, aussagekräftige Entscheidungsgrundlagen und effiziente digitale Prozesse.

Die Weiterentwicklung des Gesundheits-, Absenzen- und Case Managements sowie die konstruktive Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sozialpartner ergänzen Ihr vielseitiges Aufgabengebiet.
Sie verfügen über eine kaufmännische oder technische Grundausbildung sowie eine höhere Weiterbildung im Human Resource Management, beispielsweise als eidg. dipl. Leiter:in Human Resources, einen MAS Human Resources Management oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.

Zudem bringen Sie mehrjährige Berufs- und Führungserfahrung mit und kennen die Anforderungen eines professionell geführten HR-Bereichs aus der Praxis.

Sie sind in der operativen Umsetzung ebenso sicher wie in der konzeptionellen Weiterentwicklung, beraten überzeugend auf unterschiedlichen Hierarchiestufen und haben Veränderungs- und Digitalisierungsprojekte erfolgreich begleitet.

Sehr gute Kenntnisse in ABACUS oder fundierte Erfahrung mit einem vergleichbaren HR- und ERP-System sowie ein gutes Verständnis für betriebswirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge runden Ihr Profil ab.

Mit Ihrer integren, vertrauenswürdigen und lösungsorientierten Art gewinnen Sie Akzeptanz, führen Ihr Team wertschätzend und verbindlich und überzeugen durch Beratungskompetenz, diplomatisches Geschick und Durchsetzungsvermögen.

About Mercor
Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models.

Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.
Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner to support Mercor’s Delivery organization.
Delivery sits at the center of how Mercor turns customer demand into high-quality human data. Teams are launching and scaling accounts quickly, managing changing customer requirements, developing operators into larger roles, and making constant decisions about talent, performance and organizational structure.
The HRBP supporting this organization needs to understand that environment.
You will work directly with Delivery leaders and managers on the people decisions that affect whether an account and the organization perform: who we put in critical roles, how we develop strong operators, where management is breaking down, how teams should be structured, when someone needs a larger challenge, and when performance is below the bar.
This is not a role for someone who wants to operate at a distance from the business. You should understand the work, the customer environment and the economics well enough to challenge leaders and make practical recommendations.
Experience in the human data / AI data industry is required . You should already understand the operating model behind businesses delivering human-generated data, expert data, model evaluations, RLHF, data annotation or similar services to AI customers.

Partner directly with Delivery leadership. Advise leaders on talent, organization design, management, performance and workforce decisions as the organization scales.
Get close to the accounts. Understand the differences between teams, customers and types of work so that your people recommendations reflect the actual business rather than a generic HR model.
Raise the performance bar. Help managers distinguish exceptional performance from strong performance and performance that is below the bar. Make sure decisions are grounded in evidence and addressed quickly.
Develop strong operators. Identify high-performing SPLs, account leaders and other critical talent early. Work with leaders to create meaningful next opportunities through larger accounts, expanded scope, new problems, internal mobility or management opportunities.
Strengthen managers. Coach managers on feedback, expectations, team effectiveness, difficult conversations, performance issues and leadership behavior. Step in when a manager needs direct challenge, not simply support.
Help us retain our best people. Identify retention risk before it becomes a resignation. Understand what is driving it, including scope, compensation, manager quality, account experience, career progression and external market pull, and work with leaders on the right intervention.
Shape the organization as it changes. Partner on role clarity, organization design, succession, spans and layers, leadership changes and movement of talent between teams and accounts.
Bring a people lens to staffing and workload. Identify when persistent workload, account design, insufficient capacity or operating friction is becoming a talent problem and work with Delivery leadership to address the root cause.
Handle difficult people situations well. Support leaders through performance concerns, conduct issues, organizational changes, role changes and exits with speed, consistency and good judgment.
Run talent and performance mechanisms for Delivery. Make the company-wide approach usable in a fast-moving operating organization without turning it into unnecessary process.
See patterns before they become bigger problems. Use talent, performance, retention and employee signals to tell Delivery leadership what is changing and where intervention is needed.
Build what does not exist yet. Mercor is still early. When the business needs a new mechanism, manager tool or talent practice, you should be comfortable building the first version yourself and improving it through use.

Human data industry experience is required. You have worked inside a company delivering human data or human expertise for AI systems, including areas such as AI training data, expert data, RLHF, model evaluation, data annotation or labeling, or closely related human data operations. You understand how these businesses actually run.
8+ years of strong HRBP experience. You have been the primary People partner to senior leaders and can independently handle complex organizational and talent decisions.
Experience with operations or delivery organizations. You have supported teams where performance is closely tied to customers, quality, speed, capacity and execution.
High-growth startup experience. You are comfortable with rapid organizational change, incomplete systems, ambiguous ownership and a business that can look meaningfully different six months from now.
Strong business judgment. You can understand what is happening operationally, separate symptoms from root causes and make a clear recommendation.
High performance orientation. You are comfortable differentiating performance, investing disproportionately in exceptional people and addressing weak performance directly.

Strong talent instinct. You can recognize people with unusual trajectory, understand what may cause them to leave and help create opportunities that keep them growing.

Operator mindset. You do not stop at identifying the problem or writing the recommendation. You stay close enough to the work to make sure the solution actually works.
Direct and low ego. You communicate clearly, handle disagreement well and care more about reaching the right answer than protecting your own idea.
In-person. You are able to work from our San Francisco office five days a week.

This role has unusual proximity to the core business.

As part of our People team, you will help build and run the operational backbone that lets our people do their best work. Across the full employee lifecycle — from onboarding through to offboarding — you’ll keep day-to-day People operations running smoothly and accurately, covering areas such as onboarding, working hours, social and labour insurance, employee documentation and compliance, working closely with the wider team and our external partners.
The most exciting part of this role is that you’ll help shape our People foundations in Japan from an early stage. Rather than simply operating a finished machine, you’ll be working in an environment with plenty of white space — where the way you work directly improves how our processes and systems evolve. There’s real room here to make things better, and it’s largely yours to shape.
In a fast-growing scale-up, we’re looking for someone who enjoys more than just completing set tasks — someone who spots “this could work better” and turns it into reality. Partnering with employees, managers and external providers across a broad range of areas, you’ll naturally develop a wide, cross-functional view of People operations in Japan.

Onboarding: preparing offers and employment contracts, collecting required documents, Day 1 setup, and probation management.
Offboarding: supporting leaver processing and final pay, issuing separation and withholding certificates, equipment return and access removal.
HRIS administration: maintaining employee data, managing leave balances, producing reports, and monitoring PTO uptake.
Working hours: reconciling and operating attendance records, supporting monitoring of the 36-Agreement, and checking submissions and approvals.
Social & labour insurance: enrolments and withdrawals on hire and leave, employment insurance, standard and revised remuneration filings, and the annual labour insurance update (all handled and submitted in partnership with our external providers), plus maternity, childcare and injury/sickness benefits.
Payroll & tax: monthly coordination with our external provider and payroll team, commuting and other allowances, resident tax updates, and supporting the year-end adjustment.
Benefits & health: liaising with benefits vendors, coordinating health checks and stress checks, arranging occupational physician meetings, and setting up and following through on worksite visits.
Letters & certificates: employment contracts and terms notices, employment and salary certificates, and similar documentation.
Compliance: maintaining the employee roster and wage ledger, tracking residence status, managing fixed-term renewals, and supporting audit preparation.

The New York Times is looking for an experienced Associate HR Business Partner to support employees and managers for our Shared Services Center in Norfolk, Virginia. You will help assess organizational needs as the business continues to evolve and help set the talent strategy to address them.

You will implement programs to foster an inclusive culture in consideration of our core values and to support employee engagement, connection and career development.

As an Associate HRBP you will use your expertise across the full suite of human resources and organizational development specialties to provide strategic HR partnership and execution support.
You'll partner with the central HR teams and you will report to the Director, HR Business Partner for Central Functions. You will be in a hybrid position where you will work out of our Norfolk location 3 days per week.

Be a trusted strategic advisor and coach to department leaders, managers, and individual contributors.
Provide support to department leaders, managers, and employees, including management of annual performance/promotion and compensation processes, succession/talent programs, and oversight of process/HR administration.
Partner with Centers of Excellence to develop and deliver impactful people initiatives.
Partner with leadership to monitor how business plans and industry trends may affect talent needs, HR priorities, and the way your client groups are organized or operate.
Support the diversity, equity, and inclusion strategy of The Times by partnering with business leaders on setting priorities and monitoring progress.
Complete and process multiple HR-related transactions ensuring compliance with all internal procedures and external regulations.
Produce ad-hoc Workday reports, creating/customizing materials for central functions to identify trends and improve HR programs.
Participate in the Talent Acquisition process and Onboarding of new hires.
Partner with Employee Relations, Talent Management, and Legal teams to investigate and resolve employee relations issues, ensure regulatory compliance, and identify development needs for employees.
Complete tactical and administrative tasks, such as answering requests and inquiries from employees, and assisting with HRIS transactions.
Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

5+ years of HR experience in a Generalist or Business Partner role supporting manufacturing environments.
3+ years of experience with an HRIS such as Workday.

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or Psychology.
